_comment: Scenario-opener archetypes dealt per example by src/librarian/openerPlan.ts. `proneClass` tags a scene-skeleton-prone construction (after-action / clipped-count / object-in-motion) — openerPlan caps each prone CLASS to a minority of chapters (deal-time saturation guard) so the book-wide sweep can't flag it as cross-chapter templating. The 12 untagged archetypes are the non-prone 'spine' that fills most slots; a deal-time coverage cap keeps no single spine archetype recurring across more than a minority of chapters either (the spine-cap fix that followed the the-organized-mind / quiet runs).

openers.definition: Open in the MIDDLE of a physical action already underway — a verb in the first clause, no scene-setting preamble ("Renee slides the report back across the desk before the meeting even starts.").
Open on a line of spoken DIALOGUE (or a terse quoted instruction), then reveal who said it ("'Ship it tonight,' the director says, and the room goes quiet.").
Open on a concrete NUMBER or measurement and let it land before any context ("Forty-one tabs. That was the count when the laptop finally froze.").
Open on the RESULT or aftermath, then double back to how it happened ("The post was already deleted by the time the apology went out.").
Open on a named concrete OBJECT doing something, with the person secondary ("The dashboard turned red at 2:14, three hours after anyone last looked at it.").
Open just AFTER a decision — the character is already ACTING on a choice the reader hasn't seen ("She had already said no twice, so the third email didn't get a reply.").
Open on a specific SENSORY detail (a sound, a texture, a temperature) that grounds the scene before the task ("The phone buzzed against the wood, and the buzz was the whole problem.").
Open on a flat, declarative OBSERVATION about the situation — no character yet, just the state of things ("Every plan on the board was a week behind, and nobody had said so out loud.").

Open IN the live act of choosing — the person already in motion on one path, the choosing visible in what their hands or words are doing right now, NOT a stop-and-weigh A-vs-B binary ("Dana keys in the override while the warning box is still loading.").
Open at the instant something INTERRUPTS the person's task in progress ("Marcus is three lines into the reply when the second alert lands.").
Open on a vivid CONTRAST the person faces right now, both sides concrete ("The cleared desk sat next to the buried one, and both were hers.").

Open on one specific small physical MOTION mid-task — a reach, a pause, a set-down, a turn — that carries the moment's stakes; VARY the gesture and do NOT default to a hand or cursor hovering over a screen ("Dana sets the pen down mid-signature and slides the form back across the desk.").

Open on something the protagonist OVERHEARS — a passing remark, a half-sentence from the next desk — that reframes the moment they're in ("'They already picked someone,' someone says behind her, and Priya stops typing.").
Open on a tactile OBSTACLE met mid-task — something that jams, sticks, or won't load — forcing the next move ("The drawer jams halfway, and Sam has to decide whether the file is worth the fight.").
Open on the felt PRESSURE of a closing window AS the person works — the squeeze itself, not a clock reading ("There isn't time to read all of it, and Noah knows it, so he picks a page and commits.").
Open with the person handed a role they didn't expect to be in right now ("Nobody else volunteers, so the new hire is suddenly the one running the call.").
